title.narrative: Second Greater Mekong Subregion Tourism Infrastructure for Inclusive Growth Project

description.narrative: The project will help transform secondary towns in the Greater Mekong Subregion (GMS) eastern economic corridor into economically inclusive, competitive tourism destinations by improving transport infrastructure, urban sanitation, and capacity to sustainably manage tourism growth. It will boost trade in services by promoting cross-border tourism and deepen GMS and Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) regional cooperation and integration. About 168,000 residents are expected to benefit from climate-resilient infrastructure development, improved urban greenspace, cleaner beaches, and better access to economic opportunities.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: 1. Urban-rural access infrastructure and urban environmental services improved Indicator: 1a. 28 km of access roads to tourist sites improved Achievement: 28 Progress/Status: A total of 28 km of access roads to tourist sites has been completed across five provinces. - In Hue, the construction of 8.6 km of access roads was completed. - In Hoa Binh, 11 km of access roads was completed. - In Nghe An, the construction of a 3.7 km access road to Ru Gam Pagoda was completed. - In Quang Tri, the construction of a 368 m road linking Highway 9D to the tourist port was completed. - In Quang Binh, the construction of 4 km of roads has achieved 95% physical completion. 5% of connection to the national highway is being finalized, expected to complete by mid August 2025. Data Source: Project progress reports and project completion report

Output: 1. Urban-rural access infrastructure and urban environmental services improved Indicator: 1b. 11 passenger piers constructed or improved Achievement: 11 Progress/Status: 11 passenger piers were completed. - Hue city: 7 out of envisaged 8 piers was 100% completed. ADB loan proceeds was used to finance the access road of Le Loi pier, and the pier itself was built by a private investor's (PPC decision dated 19 February 2020). - Quang Tri, 1 of envisaged 1 pier was completed. - Quang Binh: 3 of 4 envisaged piers were completed (Than Dinh, Quang Hau, and Nhat Le). One pier (Long Dai pier) was canceled due to the selected location is within the road safety corridor of Long Dai bridge, which is not allowed following Road Traffice Law 2008. Data Source: Project progress reports and project completion report

Output: 1. Urban-rural access infrastructure and urban environmental services improved Indicator: 1c. Flood protection and drainage improved for 220-hectare urban area Achievement: 220 Progress/Status: The construction of the 4.3 km embankment and sidewalk along Cua Lo Beach in Nghe An and 1.0 km embankment and sidewalk along Nhat Le and Long Dai rivers in Quang Binh was completed. The work has contributed to flood protection and drainage improvements for an area of 220 hectares. Data Source: Project progress reports and project completion report

Output: 1. Urban-rural access infrastructure and urban environmental services improved Indicator: 1d. At least 47% of 1010 people consulted to optimize inclusiveness and gender responsiveness in project infrastructure designs are women Achievement: 47 Progress/Status: A total of 39 consultation meetings were conducted of which 472 out of 1,010 participants were female. Data Source: Project progress reports and project completion report

Output: 2. Capacity to implement ASEAN tourism standards strengthened Indicator: 2a. ASEAN tourism standards certification boards established with at least 30% women members Achievement: 43% Progress/Status: Overachieved. The ASEAN Tourism Standards Certification Board operates at the national level, certifying entities that meet ASEAN tourism standards. The Board comprises of 7 members, 4 males and 3 females. At the provincial level, the Department of Tourism acts as an advisory unit, receiving applications, conducting initial assessments, and submitting them to the national certification board for final evaluation and certification. Data Source: Project progress reports and project completion report Actual value: 43%

Output: 3. Institutional capacity for tourism destination management and infrastructure O&M strengthened Indicator: 3a. 100 public works and tourism site managers (at least 30% women) reporting increased knowledge on developing and implementing tourism management and infrastructure O&M plans Achievement: 317 Progress/Status: Overachieved.
Assigned by MCST, The Hanoi University of Culture (HUC) is implementing the destination management capacity-building activities.
1. HUC has conducted training for 317 tourism site managers and workers including 86 women (27.1%) in 4 provinces, specifically as follows: Hoa Binh: 98 (20 women) Nghe An: 152 (41 women) Quang Tri: 31 (16 women) Hue: 36 (09 women) - Names of training courses: + Training and technical training on destination development and management + Training and education on financial mechanisms, sustainable operation and maintenance of tourist destinations
2. Provide guidance on developing heritage plans and explanations (9 plans for each place) - Plan to develop a tourist destination management plan that meets international requirements - Plan to establish destination management organizations - Prepare and issue natural, historical and cultural heritage management plans - Guide and support the development of heritage explanatory documents. Data Source: Project progress reports and project completion report

Output: 3. Institutional capacity for tourism destination management and infrastructure O&M strengthened Indicator: 3b. 8 operation and maintenance plans prepared and implemented for project-supported infrastructure Achievement: 8 Progress/Status: Achieved. Total 8 O&M plans cover three infrastructures in Hue, one in Hoa Binh, one in Quang Tri, two in Nghe An, and one in Quang Binh. Data Source: Project progress reports and project completion report

Output: 3. Institutional capacity for tourism destination management and infrastructure O&M strengthened Indicator: 3c. 5 public-private partnerships established for the operation of project-supported tourism facilities. Achievement: 5 Progress/Status: Partially achieved. To date, five Private-Public Partnership (PPP) proposals have been prepared by the IAs under Hoa Binh, Quang Tri and Hue subprojects. Discussions are ongoing between the IAs and potential private operators to establish a formal engagement thus no formal arrangement has materialized. Data Source: Project progress reports and project completion report

Output: 2. Capacity to implement ASEAN tourism standards strengthened Indicator: 2b. 3 (0.35%) hotels in target provinces ASEAN Green Hotel Standard certified Achievement: 0.34% Progress/Status: Achieved. Hue has received the certification of green hotel for 3 hotels/resorts (Pilgrimage Village in 2018, Vedana Lagoon Resort & Spa in 2022, and Azerai La Residence in 2024).
For Hoa Binh, Nghe An, Quang Binh, and Quang Tri, The Departments of Tourism have implemented the dissemination and propaganda of ASEAN tourism standards as well as its benefits to all organizations/units operating in the field of tourism in the provinces.
The earlier target of 44 hotels being certified ASEAN Green Hotel Standard is not feasible because: 1. ASEAN Tourism Awards: - There are various types of awards, each with specific quotas. - Each country also has a quota (maximum of 5 awards per year), and some awards are not available annually. 2. Varying interest among tourism businesses/accommodation facilities: - The interest level of tourism businesses and accommodation facilities varies independently of state management agencies. Although MCST conducted extensive outreach, training, and promotional activities to raise service quality and awareness, participation remained limited. 3. Unfeasible design: - Four- and five-star hotels already adhere to existing standards, so obtaining ASEAN certification does not offer clear benefits to these entities. 4. Impact of COVID-19 during 2020-2022: no immediate need for certification. Data Source: Project progress reports and project completion report Actual value: 0.34%

Output: 2. Capacity to implement ASEAN tourism standards strengthened Indicator: 2c. At least 1 town in target provinces ASEAN Clean Tourist City Standard certified Achievement: 1 Progress/Status: Achieved. Hue City received the certification as a clean tourist city in 2018 and in 2024.
The earlier target of 44 hotels could not be achieved due to the limited local capacity and resources in the provinces of Hoa Binh, Nghe An, Quang Binh, and Quang Tri to meet the extensive certification criteria, which required more time and investment than initially anticipated. These provinces have implemented sanitation programs, including the installation of mobile smart toilets and environmentally friendly trash cans, to improve their infrastructure. Data Source: Project progress reports and project completion report
